$comment: Schema features a Pages document can use beyond the baseline. Every mark and block type without a feature is baseline, and a document that uses only baseline carries no stamp. A writer adds a feature's id to the document's schema.features in the same Automerge change that first writes content needing it; a reader whose build lacks an id opens the Page read-only. A mark names its feature in marks.json; a block type is listed under its feature's blocks here. model/schema-features.mjs reads this file. Add features; never remove one or reuse an id.

features.description: Host-managed named Page sources: stable source IDs bind to immutable Page-local Parquet assets and host-issued revisions. Writers use edit_page set_source.
Images with an optional dark_src alternate source and shared alternative text and title.
Strikethrough text: the strike mark, written ~~text~~ in Markdown.
Horizontal rules between blocks, written --- in Markdown.
The Page host converted the Page's preserved Markdown blocks to native rich text. A build without this feature may still write or convert preserved blocks, so it opens the Page read-only.
The Page's comments live in their own Automerge document, not in the Page document. A build without this feature would write comments into the Page document, so it opens the Page read-only.

Dataframe nodes: a block with no text whose attrs name a Page dataset asset (src, media_type, title). The viewer renders it by media type; Parquet shows as a Sift table. It has no Markdown syntax: agents write one with the insert_node operation.

A comment message's author may carry agent: { name?, model? }, what the writing client said about itself. A build without this feature would not validate the field, so it opens the comments read-only.
Local evaluation only: a dataframe node with a chart attr, a Vega-Lite spec as a JSON string. The viewer draws the node's dataset as that chart instead of a table.

Local evaluation only: a dataframe node with a source attr, a Page source ID. The viewer follows that source's current asset; src keeps the asset it held when the node was written. On a chart, every data name is a source ID.
